title: A changing night sky
info: Earth's spin makes stars rise in the east and set in the west.
Earth's orbit changes which constellations are up at night through the year.
Polaris stays nearly still in the northern sky because it lines up with Earth's axis. Most of the Southern Hemisphere cannot use it.
The Southern Cross is a famous guide in southern skies.
